posts.cooked: I made something similar; it's useful for calculating expected values but so far my experience has been that each party will have wildly different abilities so a formula doesn't really help as much as you'd think.

posts.cooked:
There’s also the issue that the average damage for any of the dice used (d4, d6, d8, d10, d12) will NOT be an integer.

 

Expected tries to kill [table] [tr][td]AtkDie↓ Lt Die→[/td][td]d4[/td][td]d6[/td][td]d8[/td][td]d10[/td][td]d12[/td][/tr] [tr][td]d4[/td][td]2.67[/td][td]6.67[/td][td]12.00[/td][td]18.67[/td][td]26.67[/td][/tr] [tr][td]d6[/td][td]4.80[/td][td]12.00[/td][td]21.60[/td][td]33.60[/td][td]48.00[/td][/tr] [tr][td]d8[/td][td]4.57[/td][td]11.43[/td][td]20.57[/td][td]32.00[/td][td]45.71[/td][/tr] [tr][td]d10[/td][td]2.67[/td][td]6.00[/td][td]10.44[/td][td]16.00[/td][td]22.67[/td][/tr] [tr][td]d12[/td][td]2.09[/td][td]4.49[/td][td]7.40[/td][td]11.03[/td][td]15.40[/td][/tr][/table]

I worked this out by count-table rather than pure formula. (makes it easier to replicate the rules - damage die ≤  lieutenant die is no drop).

The OP’s data looks closer to expected tries to step-down…
